narr: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a slow-moving cold front on March 16 across southeast Virginia. These showers and storms trained over the same areas into early on March 17, allowing for heavy rain and instances of flash flooding across portions of southeast Virginia on March 16 and 17.
ev: The 911 call center reported flooding across numerous roads in eastern Lancaster County.
VDOT reported that Route 10 was closed in eastern Prince George County west of Cabin Point Road due to high water.
VDOT reported lane closures on Route 601 in the vicinity of Laurel Springs Road due to high water.
VDOT reported delays due to standing water on I-64 East in Hampton at mile marker 267.3.
An mPING report indicated flooding in Prince George County. The report read street flooding; street/road closed; vehicle stranded.
VDOT reported that all north and south lanes were closed on Route 604 in the vicinity of Beaver Dam Road due to high water.
The public reported water over the roadway at Wilcox Neck Road and VA-3 History Land Highway.
The 911 call center reported that VA-30 was closed in West Point due to water on the roadway.
VDOT reported delays due to standing water near the intersection of Route 642 and Old Forty Road near Sussex.
An mPING report indicated street flooding near Tavern Road.
VDOT reported flooding on Route 613 at Webb Road with water over the roadway.
